title: Unexpected resource corruption when "is not" operator check
body:
### Tested versions

It was tested only on 4.4.1 Stable

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot 4.4.1 Stable

### Issue description


First of all: I'm not sure if this is a bug or my spaghetti code, as I'm new to programming. This bug doesn't cause me any problems because I've found a solution, but I was told in Discord it might be important, so I decided to report it. This is my first report, so I apologize for any inaccuracies and especially if it's not a bug and I'm just wasting your time.

I have a StatsCore class that is extend from a resource. Every creature in the game has an instance of this class. The class does a lot of different things, but it has one function that is usually not called. However, it creates an error even if it is not called when the project is initialized. In other words, the function creates an error simply by existing, and the location of the error has nothing to do with the function itself. 

Func:
### take_damage(amount) 
 if final_stats["current_hp"] <= 0:
	print("die")
		if stats_owner.get_class() != "Player": #Here bug
			print("die 2")

The error occurs in the line:
### `if stats_owner.get_class() != "Player"`

If we change this to:
### `if stats_owner is not Player:`

Then Godot stops recognizing half of the custom resources, which seems completely unrelated to this. For example, in this code in other class. This class is initialized immediately after StatsCore, and it is only available in the Player class: 
### func init_battle_ui():
	player.save_data.spell_core.update_spells()
	for a_spell in player.save_data.spell_core.active_spells:
		for icon in spell_action_grid.get_children():
			if icon is SpellPanel:
				if !icon.spell:
					icon.spell = player.save_data.spell_core.active_spells[a_spell]
					icon.init_panel(define_icon_pos(icon.spell.spell_name))
					return
In line:
### icon.spell = player.save_data.spell_core.active_spells[a_spell]
I get error: 
### Invalid assignment of property or key 'spell' with value of type 'Resource' on a base object of type 'PanelContainer (SpellPanel)'. - In the editor, this resource is recognized not as a Spell, but as a Resource without fields. 

If i'm try:
### icon.spell = player.save_data.spell_core.active_spells[a_spell] as Spell

Then it will create a correct basic instance of Spell but with default fields (so it's not [a_spell] witch we call).

At the same time, the command work perfectly: 

### icon.spell = Spell.new() 


And again, changing the check to **if stats_owner.get_class() != "Player"** in StatsCore - completely removes this behaviour. The most interesting thing is that the take_damage() method is not even called at all these stages. Function init_battle_ui(): occurs long before this method take_damage() can even be theoretically called, so I really don't understand. 

_

### I also used deep seek to describe the problem better:

1. Problem Summary
The is operator, when used to negatively check (if not x is Player) a custom class_name type, silently corrupts unrelated Resource objects in the project. This manifests as:

- Loss of exported properties: Resource instances revert to default values.
- Script detachment: Resources show as base Resource type in the inspector (losing their script association).
- No error messages: Corruption occurs silently without runtime errors or debugger warnings.
- Non-deterministic corruption: Affects unrelated resources elsewhere in the project.

### Trigger Conditions:
- Only occurs with negative checks (if not x is Player). Positive checks (if x is Player) work fine.
- Only affects custom classes (declared via class_name). Built-in types (e.g., Node2D) are unaffected.
- Corruption propagates to all loaded Resources, even those unrelated to the checked object.

### Steps to reproduce

I'm not sure how to reproduce this bug, as the "is not" operator doesn't cause problems in normal situations, and I don't even know what the exact reason is, so I don't know how to reproduce the bug, sorry

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I don't have a minimal version or a github link because my original project is very large. I could probably isolate the error by copying half of the classes, but since the error seems very disjointed, I don't know exactly what code I need to reproduce it. I couldn't think of anything better than to take all the classes that I think have an error and put them in an archive.
